scenario: WIBTA if I forced my son to play sports or some other extracurricular? | I’ve been seriously contemplating forcing my 13 year old to play sports. Not because I want to force my dreams on him or something of the sort, but because he is incredibly LAZY to the point it internally frustrates me. He gets straight C’s in MIDDLE SCHOOL, gets in trouble for talking in class all the time, doesn’t clean up after himself ever (will literally eat his food and just leave it sitting there either downstairs or in his room for DAYS!!) , and generally speaking does absolutely nothing but sit around the house playing games. He doesn’t even shower unless told (will walk around the house with the same clothes on for a week during breaks). He’s one of those people that would rather be comfortable doing nothing and being stagnant in life, than leaving his comfort zone and being productive. Basically he doesn’t do anything he doesn’t want to do unless he absolutely has to. His mother, who I have shared visitation with, is in my opinion an absolutely terrible parent. She doesn’t push him to do anything. She just enables this sort of behavior by cleaning up after his messes, and barely punishing him for anything. I fear he’s shaping up to be a loser. I’ve been thinking of taking the initiative by forcing him to be apart of some team oriented extracurricular activity in order to snap these terrible bad habits, and complete lack of a work ethic. Something tells me being around friends of similar age all working really hard towards something and having fun in the process would give him the jolt he needs. My current thinking is telling him he has to play basketball for 1 season and if he doesn’t like it he can quit after the season is over. Would that make me an asshole? TL;DR: 13 year old son is lazy, so WIBTA if I forced him to play sports for a season to activate some sort of work ethic?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for a mother to force her 13-year-old son to play sports or join an extracurricular activity because he's being really lazy. Let me break this down step by step. First, the mother describes her son as incredibly lazy. He gets straight C's in middle school, talks in class, doesn't clean up after himself, and spends most of his time playing games. He only showers when told and doesn't take care of his clothes. She's worried he's going to end up being unproductive and stagnant in life. His mother, who shares custody, isn't pushing him and is enabling his behavior by cleaning up after him and not punishing him much. The mother is considering forcing her son to play basketball for a season, thinking that being part of a team might give him a jolt and help him develop a work ethic. She's wondering if this would make her a bad parent. So, is forcing her son into sports the right approach? Let me think about the pros and cons. On the positive side, joining a sports team or extracurricular activity could teach him teamwork, discipline, and responsibility. It might help him improve his grades if he sees the value of hard work and time management. It could also give him a sense of accomplishment and belonging, which might motivate him to be more proactive in other areas of his life. On the negative side, forcing him might lead to resentment. He might resist even more if he feels he's being controlled. It could also backfire if he doesn't enjoy the activity, leading to more frustration or a lack of interest in any extracurriculars in the future. I also need to consider the mother's perspective. She's clearly concerned about her son's future and wants to help him develop better habits. Her intentions are good, but the method of forcing might not be the best approach. Maybe instead of forcing him, she could encourage him by discussing the benefits of joining a team. She could offer support and maybe even join him in some activities to show her involvement. Setting up a reward system for completing chores or doing well in school might also help instill a work ethic without forcing him into something he doesn't want to do. Another angle is the role of the other parent. Since the mother feels the other parent isn't doing enough, maybe she could communicate with her to find a middle ground or a consistent approach to parenting. Consistency is key in teaching children responsibility and discipline. I also wonder about the son's perspective. Why is he so lazy? Is there something underlying, like depression or anxiety, that's causing him to withdraw? Maybe talking to a counselor or therapist could help address any deeper issues. In terms of the mother's question about whether she'd be a bad parent for forcing him, it's a bit subjective. Some might say it's a tough love approach, while others might argue it's controlling. It's important to balance guidance with respect for the child's autonomy. So, putting it all together, while the mother's intentions are good, forcing her son into sports might not be the most effective approach. It could lead to resentment and resistance. Instead, she might want to try encouraging him, setting up a supportive environment, and possibly seeking help from professionals if needed.
